solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former boxer hurt Scotsman in company

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage, so hurt gives MAR

indicators.note: in means the Scotsman's name is placed inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: Ian is a typically Scottish man's name, the Scots form of John

explanation.surface: A retired fighter has injured a Scottish man while they were both in company.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocky Marciano was the undefeated American heavyweight champion of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky Marciano was a heavyweight champion who retired unbeaten in 1956, so he is a boxer from the past.

clue.text: Marriage completed, one changing residence?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married, used for marriage in genealogical tables
over means finished or done

explanation.surface: With the marriage finished, one partner moves out of the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relocates house moves, so the agent noun fits; the question mark flags the playful reading.

clue.text: Richard set out children's disease

parts.note: Rick is a short form of Richard

indicators.note: out indicates the letters of set are put out of order

explanation.surface: Richard explains a childhood illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like 'explained'; 'out' is the anagram signal, turning SET into ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a bone-softening condition caused by lack of vitamin D, chiefly affecting the young.

clue.text: Special invite including musical drama producing no effect

indicators.note: including means the musical drama goes inside the rearranged letters
special suggests making something unusual, so the letters of invite are reworked

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music

explanation.surface: A special invitation to a musical drama turns out to achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' makes INTIVE, and 'including' wraps it round the musical drama, which sits after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inoperative is not working or functioning, so it has no result.

clue.text: Caught infection in the end and felt sick

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word infection

parts.note: to ail is to be ill, so felt sick gives ailed

explanation.surface: Someone picked up an infection and eventually felt ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like catching an infection, but it means captured.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informal for catching or apprehending them.

clue.text: Awkward situation moderate conservatives reversed

indicators.note: reversed tells us the word for the moderate conservatives is read backwards

parts.note: in British politics, wets were the moderate Tories who opposed Thatcher's harder policies

explanation.surface: Political commentary: the moderates in the party have backtracked and left things awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' was Margaret Thatcher's dismissive name for the moderate members of her Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being in a state of worry or a predicament.

clue.text: Star won regularly on Scottish golf course

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter from star won, starting with the second

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A star golfer has won repeatedly at a famous Scottish links.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Troon, on the Ayrshire coast, regularly hosts the Open Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Troon is a championship links course in Ayrshire, west Scotland.

clue.text: Festive occasion used to be on part of boat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: was is the past of be
a sail is part of a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A celebration once took place aboard a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassail is a festive drinking and carol-singing revel, traditionally at Christmas.

clue.text: Award winner is carrying Oscar shakily

parts.note: a victor is the winner of a contest

indicators.note: carrying means the word is holds the shaken-up letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: shakily signals that the letters of Oscar are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prizewinner nervously clutches the Oscar statuette they have just received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shakily' makes ACROS and 'carrying' wraps the clue's 'is' round it. Jumbling 'carrying Oscar' whole is the tempting false path, but the letters do not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military decoration for gallantry, an honour given to the brave.

clue.text: Insect larva to provide food on tall upright rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to cater is to supply food for an event
a pillar is a tall column, here of rock

explanation.surface: A grub feeds itself on a tall standing stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the larval stage of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: Former bailiff concerned about first female

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning, as in a letter heading
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A historical estate officer is worried about the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English official who managed a manor or district on behalf of a lord.

clue.text: One not returning into rough sea somewhere on the Baltic

indicators.note: into means the reversed piece is placed inside the jumbled sea
rough suggests disturbed water, so the letters of sea are churned up
returning means one plus not is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor who never comes home has gone into stormy waters somewhere in the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns INOT into TONI, which 'into' places inside ESA, the result of 'rough' rearranging SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a country on the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea, so it is a place located there.

clue.text: Kitty, after quantity of money, brought back wine

indicators.note: after places the cat piece following the reversed money piece
brought back means the word for the amount of money is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
kitty is a pet name for a cat

explanation.surface: The pooled kitty, after some money was spent, brought back wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' looks like a pool of shared money, which fits 'quantity of money'; here it is the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a sweet white wine made from the muscat grape, especially in southern France.

clue.text: Sailor runs into sea, outwardly eager

indicators.note: into means the runs abbreviation goes inside the sea word

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: outwardly asks for the outside letters of eager

explanation.surface: An eager seaman runs headlong into the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is literary for the high sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who navigates or works on a ship.

clue.text: Expert training learner to drive forward

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
PE is physical education, i.e. physical training
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A professional instructor teaches a learner driver to move off.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to push or drive something onward, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Criticise novel ploy for full suit of armour

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of ploy are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A critic slams an inventive scheme for a complete set of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply was originally a complete set of a warrior's armour, now any impressive array.

clue.text: Patterned knitwear dear — fogy able to get half off repeatedly

indicators.note: removing the first half of each of the words dear, fogy and able in turn leaves their second halves

explanation.surface: A dear old fuddy-duddy can buy patterned knitwear at half price, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word loses its first half, leaving AR, GY and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyle is a diamond-check knitting pattern, typical of socks and sweaters, named after a Scottish clan.

clue.text: More boisterous argument with the German and Republican

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel
die is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A noisier quarrel breaks out with the German and an American Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy means noisy and disorderly, and the comparative form describes being more unruly.

clue.text: Women's Institute radical connected to the internet?

parts.note: WI is the Women's Institute, a British community organisation for women
a red is a left-wing radical

explanation.surface: Asks whether the Women's Institute's radical member is online.
explanation.definitionFit: Wired is informal for linked up to computer networks; the question mark marks the loose sense.

clue.text: Pub having the wow factor, don't you think?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
it is the special quality of someone who has the wow factor, as in an It girl

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pub has real wow factor.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang, a contraction of 'isn't it' used as a general tag question.
explanation.definitionFit: This colloquial tag seeks agreement at the end of a remark, like saying 'right?' or 'isn't that so?'

clue.text: Stunner modelled again, maybe, on return

indicators.note: on return means the assembled pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re- as a prefix means again
an artist's model sits, so modelled gives sat

explanation.surface: A beauty posed once more, perhaps, on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' flags that modelling is just one example of sitting. 'Stunner' looks like a beauty, but it is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun that incapacitates its target.

clue.text: Where novices ski, carer with line's adapted poles

parts.note: a nurse is someone who cares for the sick
RY is short for railway, a line, and the apostrophe s adds an S

indicators.note: adapted means the letters of poles are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A carer and a ski line have modified poles for the beginners.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginners learn on the gentle, easy runs at a ski resort, given a name suggesting a children's room.

clue.text: From Truro, Denis travelled by horse

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words Truro, Denis, running across the comma

explanation.surface: Denis, from the Cornish city of Truro, made his journey on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Truro is the county town of Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who journeyed on horseback rode, the past tense of ride.

clue.text: Perhaps salver coated in ale and grass

indicators.note: coated in means the salver word sits inside the ale word

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
a salver is an example of a tray, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A serving tray gets covered with spilt ale and grass cuttings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like lawn, but it is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informer, someone who betrays others.
